claims.text: The material family of interest is multiphase refractory high-entropy alloys containing BCC and B2 phases.
The primary mechanical property of interest is room-temperature ductility, measured through elongation to failure or deformation before fracture.
BCC/B2 RHEAs will exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr can exist as a largely single-phase BCC alloy with weak B2 ordering after solutionizing and quenching.
Isothermal aging between 600 K and 1000 K for 100 to 1000 hours will induce chemical ordering and phase evolution in the proposed alloys.
Aging below the order-disorder transition temperature can activate diffusion-mediated chemical ordering.
A disordered or weakly ordered BCC matrix permits dislocation-mediated deformation and high ductility.
A coherent B2/BCC composite can remain ductile through interphase deformation synergy or TRIP.
Coherent interfaces can facilitate dislocation transfer, reduce interfacial stress concentration, and suppress cracking.
A continuous or incoherent B2 phase can cause strain localization or brittle fracture.
TRIP approaches are ineffective in inherently brittle Al-containing RHEAs that fracture without appreciable strain localization.
Dissolution, severe coarsening, coherency loss, or transformation of B2 at extended aging times or higher temperatures will restore matrix ductility.
Negative chemical short-range-order parameters indicate ordering and a tendency to form intermetallic compounds.
SRO values approaching zero indicate homogenization at the order-disorder transition.
The W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy considered in the cited simulation has a predicted ODTT of approximately 1120 K.
The ductility transition is bounded by the alloy-specific ODTT and by a critical B2 volume fraction needed to form a continuous brittle network.
The proposed non-monotonic transition is limited to systems in which B2 is metastable and can dissolve or coarsen substantially during aging.
Room-temperature ductility versus aging time will have a U- or W-shaped profile, with an intermediate minimum followed by recovery.
Condition 2 of Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr maintains high ductility because it is largely single-phase BCC.
A fully ordered brittle alloy will remain brittle throughout aging.

contradictions.description: The baseline describes Condition 2 as having no ordering tendency, whereas the initial-state description and cited evidence characterize the same condition as having weak B2 ordering.

The structural mediator invokes TRIP as a source of ductility in the coherent B2/BCC state, while the cited RHEA mechanism states that TRIP is not applicable to inherently brittle Al-containing RHEAs; the scope distinguishing these cases is not defined.
